title: When the Spire Turns
premise: In the city of Vellamark, magic was outlawed fifteen years ago, and Noor Halloran has survived by hiding their beast-speaker gift behind a stall of harmless charms. When the crown's new hunt exposes them, Noor flees into the undercity and finds the smugglers, exiles, and talking animals who become the family they never had. Together they uncover the truth: the king died years ago, and something ancient wearing his crown has been feeding on the city's bound magics. To save Vellamark, Noor must break the binding at the Spire's heart, choosing justice outside the law over safety, and inherit not a throne but a responsibility shared with everyone they love.
about_author: S. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to things that could not speak back. They write about outsiders, animal minds, and the quiet violence of laws that decide who counts as human.

chapters.title: Charms for Small Coin
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A day in the market: selling luck-knots, quietly bargaining with a lame cart-horse, hiding the thrill of being understood. The emotional beat is the ache of a gift used only in whispers, establishing what Noor stands to lose.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Criers announce the crown's hunt for 'the gifted,' offering silver for names. A neighbor Noor once helped looks at them too long. Fear curdles into the first decision: pack the satchel, free the caged wren, run.

chapters.title: Down the Drowned Stair
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, pursued through rooftops by hunters' hounds who, heartbreakingly, are ordered to hunt kin. A sewer-rat guides them to a hidden stair. The beat is betrayal of the body's own panic and the first taste of the undercity's strange mercy.

chapters.title: The Tallow Market
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Beneath Vellamark, exiles trade in unbound magic: a moth-reading fortune teller, a boy who speaks to rust. Noor meets Brannic, a one-armed former royal falconer, who offers shelter but no trust yet.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The undercity's rats describe a pale procession carrying a sleeping king down into the Spire years ago. Noor realizes the hunt isn't about control; it's harvest. Dread replaces fear as the stakes widen beyond survival.

chapters.title: Brannic's Oath
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Flashback to the night he lost his arm and his king's sanity in the same hour, sworn to silence by terror. He tells Noor the truth he buried. The beat is guilt finally given words, and two strangers becoming conspirators.

chapters.title: A Family Assembled
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The found family forms around a plan: Sefa the moth-reader, Pip the rust-boy, Old Marrow the rat-matriarch, Brannic. Warmth amid danger; Noor, orphaned long ago, feels belonging for the first time and fears its cost.

chapters.title: The Hunt Comes Below
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Crown wardens breach the Tallow Market; the community scatters through flood tunnels. Pip is taken. The beat is grief sharpened into resolve, and the discovery that the wardens' hounds hesitate when Noor speaks to them.

chapters.title: Crown and Cage
chapters.summary: Pip's POV, imprisoned in the Spire's vaults among caged gifted folk whose magic drains upward through copper roots. He learns the thing on the throne eats slowly, keeping victims alive. Horror, but also hope: the prisoners are organizing.

chapters.title: The Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The freed wren returns bearing word from the city's birds: the palace ravens know a way in, but demand a price, a truth spoken aloud that Noor has never confessed. The beat is the cost of honesty before the cost of blood.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Confession scene: Noor admits they once spoke to the old queen's dying hawk and said nothing as the 'king' changed, believing themselves a coward. The family absorbs it without judgment. Grief becomes fuel.

chapters.title: Ink and Copper
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Planning the infiltration using his old falconer's knowledge of the Spire's mews and the ravens' map. Sefa reads moths for omens that contradict each other. Tension of the eve-of-battle kind, laced with tenderness.

chapters.title: Up Through the Mews
chapters.summary: Noor and Brannic's POV, alternating. The ascent through the rookery, past sleeping wardens, guided by raven whispers. Near-discovery forces Noor to still a guard dog with a spoken promise instead of a command. Mercy as tactic.

chapters.title: The Sleeping King
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the vaults they find the real king, alive, hollowed, dreaming inside a lattice of copper. He recognizes Brannic. The revelation lands: rescue is possible, but waking him may kill him. Impossible choice number one.

chapters.title: The Thing That Wears Him
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV, unnamed. The crown-entity senses intrusion, reflects on centuries of wearing rulers, and decides the city has ripened for full consumption. Cold, patient menace; the reader sees how small the heroes truly are.

chapters.title: Riot of Small Voices
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Noor calls every beast in the Spire, rats, hounds, ravens, the warden's own horses, and the building shakes. Pip frees the cages from within. Chaos as liberation; the lawless rising all at once.

chapters.title: The Spire Turns
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax begins. At the crown-room, the entity offers Noor inheritance: wear me, rule kindly, I only want a willing host. Noor nearly accepts, seeing a world where beasts and outcasts are heard. Temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax. Refusing the crown, Noor does the opposite of seizing power: they unbind it, speaking every name the entity has stolen, giving the magic back to the crowd below. The entity unravels screaming. Sacrifice over sovereignty.

chapters.title: What Waking Costs
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. The true king wakes diminished, mortal, remembering nothing of his lost years, and must face what was done in his name. He abdicates rather than rebuild the machinery that hunted children. Justice without vengeance.

chapters.title: After the Hunt
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The city reckons: wardens disarmed, some forgiven, some not. The gifted emerge blinking into daylight. Not everything mends; Pip carries scars, Marrow doesn't survive the riot. Mourning braided with cautious dawn.

chapters.title: The Open Stall
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Rebuilding the market above ground, openly, charms beside beast-speech, the cart-horse now a partner not a secret. The king, plain-clothed, buys a luck-knot and asks nothing. Quiet joy; inheritance redefined as stewardship.

chapters.title: When the Spire Turns Again
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue. Years later, Noor teaches a new generation of speakers beneath the Spire, which now turns as a windmill grinding grain for the city. The last line: power kept is power that rots; power shared is the only crown worth wearing.
